title: When History Returns: Hybrid Management of Syphilitic Aortitis Causing Severe Aortic Arch Branch Stenosis and Cerebral Hypoperfusion.
authors: Julia Al Mousli; Anders Håkanson; Jonas Malmstedt; David Lindström
abstract:
Cardiovascular manifestations of tertiary syphilis are rare in the antibiotic era, but important to consider in atypical vascular findings. These manifestations typically appear several years after the primary infection and may lead to structural damage in the cardiovascular system, requiring surgical intervention despite appropriate antibiotic therapy.
This case describes a rare manifestation of cardiovascular syphilis in a 46 year old woman presenting with dizziness, pre-syncope, and syncope consistent with global cerebral ischaemia. Extensive evaluation revealed syphilitic aortitis with severe stenosis and or occlusion of all the major aortic arch branches. The patient was managed with antibiotic therapy in combination with surgical revascularisation. Both endovascular and open surgical approaches were used to restore blood flow to the left common carotid, left vertebral, and left subclavian arteries. This intervention improved cerebral perfusion and resolved the patient's symptoms. At two years, the carotid stent was patent, while the carotid subclavian bypass was occluded. The patient remained free from cerebral ischaemic symptoms but reported bilateral arm claudication.
Tertiary syphilis should be considered as a differential diagnosis when atypical arterial disease is encountered. Hybrid revascularisation may provide an effective, less invasive treatment strategy.

title: Impact of True and False Lumen Origins on Target Vessel Instability in Post-Dissection F/BEVAR.
authors: Vivian C Gomes; Mark A Farber; Adam W Beck; Matthew J Eagleton; Gustavo S Oderich; Lucas R Kanamori; Bruno Schmid; Andres Schanzer; Matthew P Sweet; Sara L Zettervall; Carlos H Timaran; Xingsheng Li; Ryan S Cantor; F Ezequiel Parodi; U.S. Aortic Research Consortium
abstract:
To evaluate the occurrence of target artery-related adverse events in post-dissection F/BEVAR patients, based upon artery origin from the true or false lumen.
This is a multicenter, prospective, cohort study evaluating post-dissection patients treated with F/BEVAR, in the US Aortic Research Consortium. The primary endpoint was 5-year target vessel instability (TVI). Secondary endpoints included 5-year primary patency, freedom from secondary interventions (SIs), and type Ic and IIIc endoleaks. The analysis was performed on a per-vessel basis.
A total of 1052 target arteries were analyzed, primarily including the celiac, superior mesenteric, and renal arteries, with individual hepatic and splenic arteries occasionally incorporated in the repair. Of the 277 patients included, 75% were men, and 19% were black, with a mean age of 66.8 ± 10.3 years. The mean aneurysm sac diameter was 66.0 ± 11.4 mm, with extent II thoracoabdominal aneurysms being the most prevalent (72.6%) among this cohort. Technical success was obtained in 96% of the cases. As primary outcome, the incidence of target vessel instability (TVI) was significantly lower (P<0.001) among the true-lumen vessels (16.4%) compared to false-lumen (29.9%) and dual-lumen arteries (43.8%). As for the secondary outcomes, the incidence of type Ic endoleak was significantly higher (P=0.001) in false-lumen vessels (9.6%) and dual-lumen vessels (8.6%) compared to true-lumen vessels (3.3%). There was no significant difference in the incidence of type IIIc endoleak (p=0.241) or target vessel occlusion (P=0.458). Target artery stenosis was significantly more common among arteries originating from the false lumen compared to true lumen (2.6% vs 0.4%, P=0.009). Fenestrations were associated with a higher incidence (30.5%) of TVI when compared to branches (5.9% P=0.005), however, this was observed only among dual-lumen vessels. Arteries incorporated by a fenestration and that had a dual-lumen origin, were associated with a higher occurrence of secondary interventions (23.7%) compared to true-lumen vessels (8.6%, P=0.010). The same was not observed among the arteries incorporated by a branch configuration. The time-to-event analysis demonstrated a significantly higher 5-year freedom from TVI in true-lumen vessels compared to false and dual-lumen ones (True lumen: 83.6%; False=70.1 %; Dual=56.2 %; Log-rank P=0.0002). Freedom from secondary interventions at 5 years was significantly higher in true-lumen vessels compared to dual-lumen ones (Log-rank P=0.0104), but not to false-lumen arteries (Log-rank P=0.0847). The 5-year primary patency did not differ significantly among groups (True lumen: 98.3%; False = 92.6%; Dual=93.9%; Log-rank P=0.1368). On Cox proportional hazards analysis, dual-lumen (95% CI 1.24-3.28, p=0.005) and false-lumen (95% CI 1.04 - 2.60, p=0.0325) target arteries were associated with an increased hazard of TVI, when compared to true lumen arteries, having 2.02 (P=0.005) and 1.65 (P=0.0325) times more risk of presenting TVI than a true-lumen vessel CONCLUSIONS: In F/BEVAR for post-dissection aneurysms, target vessel instability and secondary intervention are significantly lower in target arteries originating from the true lumen, when compared to false-lumen or dual-lumen vessels. Device design, with use of fenestrations or branches may also play a role, with a significant difference only observed in dual-lumen target arteries.

title: Post-mortem CT angiography for fatal vascular lesions in forensic death investigation: a systematic review of diagnostic performance, added value, and pitfalls.
authors: Luca Marinelli; Fiammetta Cappabianca; Salvatore Cappabianca
abstract:
Post-mortem CT angiography (PMCTA) is increasingly used in forensic death investigation to assess vascular disease, haemorrhage, and traumatic or natural vascular causes of death. However, its practical value depends on the lesion being investigated, the angiographic protocol, and the way imaging findings are integrated with autopsy and pathology. This systematic review evaluated the diagnostic performance, added value, and main pitfalls of PMCTA for fatal vascular lesions.
PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane/CENTRAL were searched for human post-mortem studies evaluating PMCTA in forensic, medico-legal, coronial, or post-mortem settings. Eligible studies compared PMCTA with autopsy, histopathology, targeted vascular dissection, or autopsy-based consensus. Evidence was grouped according to practical forensic use, including coronary stenosis assessment, autopsy triage, global vascular lesion detection, haemorrhage-source localization, aortic or traumatic vascular injury assessment, coronary plaque characterization, and artifact-related pitfalls. Risk of bias was assessed using a QUADAS-2-based approach adapted to forensic PMCTA studies.
The available evidence did not support unrestricted pooling of all fatal vascular lesions. PMCTA was used for different forensic questions, and only coronary stenosis provided data close to conventional diagnostic accuracy assessment. In this domain, available studies showed high specificity but only moderate sensitivity for critical stenosis. Autopsy-triage studies suggested that PMCTA may reduce or guide invasive autopsy in selected adult coronial workflows. Global comparison studies showed added value for vascular lesion detection, and haemorrhage-source studies suggested that PMCTA may help localize bleeding vessels. Evidence on fatal coronary plaque characterization is emerging. Pitfall studies showed that post-mortem clots, incomplete vascular filling, contrast leakage, and extravasation artifacts may mimic or obscure vascular pathology.
PMCTA is best interpreted as a complementary tool in forensic vascular death investigation rather than as a general substitute for autopsy. Its contribution is strongest when it answers a specific vascular question, such as documenting coronary stenosis, guiding autopsy, mapping vascular lesions, localizing haemorrhage, or supporting targeted histopathology. Careful correlation with autopsy, pathology, case circumstances, and protocol-related artifacts remains essential.

title: Impact of Right Heart Damage on the Prognostic Value of LV Mass Regression After TAVR.
authors: Hyun Jin Ahn; Jeehoon Kang; Minju Han; Seokhun Yang; Doyeon Hwang; Jung-Kyu Han; Han-Mo Yang; Kyung-Woo Park; Hyun-Jae Kang; Bon-Kwon Koo; Hyo-Soo Kim
abstract:
Left ventricular mass index (LVMI) regression after aortic valve replacement is associated with myocardial recovery and improved outcomes, but its prognostic relevance in advanced cardiac damage, particularly right heart involvement, is uncertain.
The authors aimed to determine whether the prognostic relevance of LVMI regression after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) differs according to right heart damage.
We retrospectively analyzed data from 548 patients with severe aortic stenosis who underwent TAVR between 2011 and 2023. Extravalvular cardiac damage was staged by echocardiography as stages 0 to 2 (no right heart damage) or stages 3 to 4 (right heart damage). LVMI regression was defined as a reduction from baseline to 1 month after TAVR. The primary composite endpoint was cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization.
Among the cohort (median age 81.0 [77.0-85.0] years; 51.3% women [281/548]), 9.1% (50/548) exhibited right heart damage. LVMI decreased after TAVR in both groups. Over a median follow-up of 1,020 (Q1-Q3: 552-1,731) days, LVMI regression was associated with lower risk of the primary endpoint in patients without right heart damage (adjusted HR: 0.59; 95% CI: 0.36-0.97; P = 0.04), whereas no association was observed in those with right heart damage (adjusted HR: 1.58; 95% CI: 0.40-6.27; P = 0.51) (P for interaction = 0.47).
Although LVMI regression occurred after TAVR regardless of right heart involvement, an association with improved clinical outcomes was observed in patients without right heart damage but not in those with right heart damage; however, given the nonsignificant interaction test, this finding should be considered hypothesis-generating.

title: Anatomically high-risk features, functionally benign: CT-FFR-guided assessment of coronary artery anomalies-case report.
authors: Şevval İlke Ebeoğlu; İpek Aydın; Abdullah Ömer Ebeoğlu; Ahmet Yıldız; Diaa Abdel Hakim; Emir Barış Özgür Ökçün
abstract:
Anomalous aortic origin of a coronary artery (AAOCA) can show anatomically high-risk features on coronary computed tomographic angiography (CCTA), yet ischaemia may be dynamic and not proportional to anatomic appearance. Computed tomographic-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR) provides lesion-specific physiologic information from routine CCTA datasets and may aid management when anatomy and symptoms are discordant.
We describe three adults evaluated with CCTA and adjunct CT-FFR (DeepVessel FFR). Case 1: a 61-year-old asymptomatic man with anomalous right coronary artery (RCA) origin from the left coronary sinus and an interarterial course; CT-FFR 0.94-0.95 and normal myocardial perfusion scintigraphy supported conservative management. Case 2: a 23-year-old woman with intermittent, non-exertional chest discomfort and a family history of sudden cardiac death; CCTA showed a rare left main coronary artery origin from the non-coronary sinus with a retroaortic course; CT-FFR remained >0.80 (left anterior descending [LAD] 0.87; left circumflex [LCX] 0.88) and intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) excluded left main coronary artery (LM) ostial stenosis (minimum lumen area [MLA] 11 mm2). Case 3: a 50-year-old asymptomatic man with an anomalous RCA from the left coronary sinus and an interarterial course; CT-FFR nadir was 0.87, and Heart Team discussion supported conservative management. Follow-up (6-12 months) was uneventful.
CT-FFR may complement anatomic assessment in selected adults with AAOCA and help avoid unnecessary invasive testing. However, because CT-FFR is derived from resting CCTA it cannot exclude exertion-dependent dynamic compression; persistent concern should prompt stress testing and/or invasive physiologic and intravascular assessment.

title: Ventricularis delamination causing acute left main obstruction during TAVI: a case report.
authors: Bo Fu; Fenlong Xue; Xiquan Song; Qingliang Chen; Nan Jiang
abstract:
Acute coronary obstruction is a rare but potentially fatal complication of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), most commonly resulting from displacement of a calcified native leaflet. We describe an unusual mechanism involving delamination of native aortic leaflet tissue with subsequent coronary ostial obstruction.
An 80-year-old woman with severe symptomatic calcific aortic stenosis underwent transfemoral TAVI with a self-expanding valve. During valve deployment, she developed abrupt haemodynamic collapse with marked ST-segment elevation. Emergency angiography demonstrated acute left main coronary obstruction, while transoesophageal echocardiography revealed a newly developed mobile flap-like structure in the ascending aorta, raising concern for acute aortic dissection. Emergency surgical exploration excluded aortic dissection and demonstrated delamination of native aortic leaflet tissue, macroscopically considered to involve the ventricularis layer. The detached tissue had prolapsed into the left coronary ostium, causing mechanical obstruction of coronary inflow. Excision of the obstructing tissue and surgical aortic valve replacement restored coronary perfusion.
This case expands the mechanistic spectrum of TAVI-related coronary obstruction and highlights an important diagnostic pitfall. Native leaflet delamination may produce a mobile intra-aortic flap mimicking acute aortic dissection while simultaneously causing catastrophic coronary obstruction. Recognition of this rare mechanism may facilitate prompt diagnosis and appropriate rescue intervention.

title: A Novel Intraluminal Microtube Anastomosis System (IMAS) for Rapid Rat Microvascular Reconstruction: Development and Experimental Evaluation.
authors: Sam-Youl Yoon
abstract: Background/Objectives: Conventional interrupted microvascular anastomosis is technically demanding and time-consuming. We developed an intraluminal microtube anastomosis system (IMAS) in which circumferential anchoring ridges on the outer surface mechanically retain each arterial end while two external circumferential ligatures secure the reconstruction. This study compared IMAS with conventional interrupted microsurgical anastomosis in a rat infrarenal abdominal aortic model. Methods: Forty male Sprague Dawley rats (250-300 g) were allocated to IMAS (n = 20) or conventional interrupted microsurgical anastomosis (n = 20). Random-sequence generation and allocation concealment were handled by an animal-experiment assistant. All formal procedures were performed by the same surgeon, who was proficient in conventional microsuturing and had completed 10 pilot IMAS procedures before the study. Anastomosis time was measured from complete aortic transection to restoration of flow after clamp removal. Patency was assessed at 1 week and 1 month by color Doppler ultrasonography, with terminal gross examination at 1 month. The study was exploratory and was not powered as a patency non-inferiority or equivalence study. Results: Mean anastomosis time was 5 min 30 s ± 60 s with IMAS and 20 min 32 s ± 75 s with conventional suturing (p < 0.001). The between-group mean difference (conventional minus IMAS) was 902 s (95% CI, 859-945 s), corresponding to an approximately 73% reduction. Patency was 19/20 (95%) in both groups at 1 week (p = 1.000) and 18/20 (90%) in both groups at 1 month (p = 1.000). No gross device migration, aneurysmal dilatation, or anastomotic leakage was observed in patent IMAS-treated vessels at necropsy. Conclusions: In this exploratory rat model, IMAS substantially shortened reconstruction time. The observed short-term patency proportions were the same in the two groups, but the study was not sufficiently powered to establish equivalence or non-inferiority in patency. Histological response, lumen stenosis, quantitative flow, mechanical strength, material biocompatibility, and longer-term outcomes require further evaluation.

title: The Fate of Mitral Valve Regurgitation After TAVI.
authors: Karin Steiner; Melchior Burri; Nina Feirer; Tobias Rheude; Hendrik Ruge; Markus Krane; Keti Vitanova
abstract: Background: Outcomes of patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) for severe aortic stenosis with concomitant severe mitral regurgitation (MR) remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to quantify the evolution of high-grade MR after TAVI, compare changes using MR etiology, and assess associations between MR etiology, early improvement, or residual discharge MR and mortality. Methods: In a retrospective single-center cohort, 112 TAVI patients with baseline more-than-moderate MR were included (functional n = 94; degenerative n = 18). MR grade was assessed pre-TAVI, at discharge, and at last available follow-up (serial studies up to ≥5 years), and 5-year all-cause mortality was analyzed. Results: At discharge, 34% of patients improved by more than one MR grade, and 26% by one grade. Among 45 patients with available late echocardiographic follow-up, 62% improved by more than one grade, 24% by one grade. Exploratory five-year survival analyses did not demonstrate a significant difference for MR etiology (p = 0.23), discharge MR grade (p = 0.11), or MR improvement status (p = 0.12). Conclusions: Among patients surviving to longitudinal echocardiographic follow-up, MR reduction was frequently observed after TAVI. Exploratory analyses did not demonstrate statistically significant differences in 5-year survival according to MR etiology, early MR improvement, or discharge MR severity. However, limited sample size and incomplete follow-up preclude definitive prognostic conclusions. Overall, these findings are compatible with a surveillance-first management, and with individualized consideration of adjunctive mitral therapy for persistent higher-grade symptomatic MR.

title: Self-Expanding Stent-Assisted Reconstruction of Distal Supra-Aortic Vessels in Acute Type A Aortic Dissection: A Comparative Analysis.
authors: Bowen Li; Feng Shi; Zhipeng Hu; Zongli Ren; Zhiyong Wu; Luocheng Li; Zhiwei Wang
abstract: Background: Supra-aortic vessel reconstruction during total aortic arch replacement in acute Stanford type A aortic dissection patients with dissected distal supra-aortic vessels remains technically challenging; proximal supra-aortic vessel replacement alone carries a high risk of neurological complications secondary to intimal inversion. This study aims to evaluate clinical outcomes of self-expanding stent-assisted supra-aortic vessel reconstruction compared with proximal replacement of supra-aortic vessels alone. Methods and Results: We performed a single-center retrospective comparative analysis of 49 consecutive patients undergoing emergency total aortic arch replacement for acute Stanford type A aortic dissection from January 2022 to December 2023. Patients were divided into two groups according to intraoperative anatomy and surgeon decision: self-expanding stent-assisted supra-aortic vessel reconstruction (SAVR, n = 26) and proximal replacement of supra-aortic vessels alone (PRVA, n = 23). Neurological outcomes related to supra-aortic vessel intimal inversion, operative parameters, blood product transfusion, and short-term complications were analyzed. The mean follow-up was 18.2 ± 4.1 months (range, 12-24 months). The SAVR group exhibited significantly lower supra-aortic vessel stenosis rate (3.8% vs. 30.4%, p < 0.001) and zero cases of intimal inversion-related luminal collapse versus five cases in the PRVA group (0 vs. 5, p = 0.02). Numerically fewer cases of symptomatic stroke (0% vs. 8.7%, p = 0.09) and radiographic cerebral infarction (3.8% vs. 13.0%, p = 0.17) were observed in the SAVR group, though the differences did not achieve statistical significance. Red blood cell and fresh frozen plasma transfusion requirements, mechanical ventilation duration, and ICU stay length were significantly lower in the SAVR cohort. Cardiopulmonary bypass time and 30-day mortality were comparable between groups. Conclusions: Self-expanding stent-assisted supra-aortic vessel reconstruction represents a promising technical option during total arch replacement for acute Stanford type A aortic dissection with distal supra-aortic dissection, associated with superior branch vessel patency and favorable numerical trends in neurological and recovery-related endpoints, with a comparable early-term safety profile. Potential benefits require further validation in larger cohorts.

title: Staged Management with Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in a Patient with ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction, Low-Gradient Aortic Stenosis, and Recurrent Cardiogenic Shock: A Case Report.
authors: Zhongheng Li; Weili Teng; Ruining Li; Liyun He; Dan Li; Lincheng Yang; Mengsha Gao; Ling Xu; Yupeng Wang; Ming Cui; Lijie Sun
abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Cardiogenic shock after successful culprit-vessel revascularization may remain multifactorial when important structural heart disease coexists. Case Presentation: We report an 81-year-old man with extensive anterior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction, low-gradient calcific aortic stenosis (AS) with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, and cardiogenic shock. Primary percutaneous coronary intervention of a completely occluded proximal left anterior descending artery was performed under intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) support. Echocardiography showed an aortic valve area of 0.53 cm2, a mean transvalvular gradient of 25 mmHg, and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 32%. Although the findings raised concern for a classical low-flow, low-gradient AS phenotype, the low-flow state and true-severe AS could not be formally confirmed because stroke-volume index, dobutamine stress echocardiography, and standardized CT calcium scoring were unavailable. After IABP removal on day 6, profound recurrent shock with lactic acidosis and multiorgan hypoperfusion developed on day 10. IABP reinsertion was followed by improvement in systemic perfusion, whereas brief trial-off periods reproduced hemodynamic and symptomatic deterioration. TAVR was performed on day 24 after recovery of end-organ function, discontinuation of vasoactive drugs, partial platelet recovery, and completion of CT-based procedural planning. IABP was removed the next day, and the patient was discharged on day 30 with an ejection fraction of 42%. Conclusions: Recurrent shock after successful culprit-vessel reperfusion should prompt reassessment for persistent structural hemodynamic burdens. Temporary support may serve as a bridge to recovery and individualized procedural planning in selected patients, but the observed improvement after TAVR represents a temporal association in a multifactorial shock state and should not be interpreted as evidence for routine IABP use in infarct-related cardiogenic shock or a predetermined delay before valve intervention.

title: Short- and Mid-Term Effects of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement on Heart Rate Variability in Patients With Aortic Valve Stenosis.
authors: Emre Pacaci; Abdullah Yildirim; Mert Evlice; Guluzar Tras; Cuma Suleymanoglu; Muhammet Salih Ates; Mukremin Coskun; Emre Sezici; Mustafa Ozan Gursoy; Omer Sen; Omer Genc; Ibrahim Halil Kurt
abstract:
Heart rate variability (HRV) reflects autonomic nervous system balance and has emerged as a potential prognostic marker in cardiovascular diseases. However, the relationship between HRV and mortality following transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) remains unclear.
This prospective cohort study included 230 patients with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis who underwent TAVR between June 2022 and June 2024. Twenty-four-hour Holter electrocardiography recordings were obtained one day before and at 3 months after the procedure to assess HRV using both time- and frequency-domain parameters.
Among the 230 patients enrolled, the 12-month all-cause mortality rate was 14.3%. Among frequency-domain parameters, the pre-TAVR low frequency/high frequency (LF/HF) ratio improved markedly from 2.20±1.45 to 1.54±0.85 (p<0.001). In the time domain, standard deviation of NN intervals (89-103 ms, p=0.027), standard deviation of the averages of NN intervals (68-83 ms, p=0.003), and percentage of successive RR intervals (10.0%-12.0%, p=0.036) all showed significant improvements, while root mean square of successive RR interval differences remained unchanged. The pre-TAVR LF/HF ratio was significantly lower in survivors and provided the best discrimination for 1-year mortality prediction (area under the curve 0.815; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.750-0.881). Calibration analysis confirmed excellent predictive accuracy (C-index, 0.81; Brier score, 0.104; pseudo-R2, 0.285). Patients with a pre-TAVR LF/HF ratio>1.34 had significantly lower mortality at follow-up (hazard ratio [HR] 0.103; 95% CI 0.042-0.250; log-rank p<0.001), and this association remained significant in landmark analysis beyond 3 months (HR 0.163; log-rank p<0.001).
HRV parameters provide meaningful prognostic information in patients undergoing TAVR. Among them, a reduced pre-TAVR LF/HF ratio is independently associated with increased 1-year mortality and may serve as a practical, non-invasive marker for risk stratification.

title: Association Between Revascularization Timing and Outcomes for Coronary Artery Disease in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation.
authors: Masashi Yamaguchi; Futoshi Yamanaka; Koki Shishido; Noriaki Moriyama; Tomoki Ochiai; Hirokazu Miyashita; Yoichi Sugiyama; Daisuke Sato; Eiji Koyama; Kunihiko Shimizu; Kazuki Tobita; Takashi Matsumoto; Shingo Mizuno; Yutaka Tanaka; Masato Murakami; Shigeru Saito
abstract:
Coronary artery disease (CAD) is common in patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS), yet the optimal timing of coronary revascularization in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) remains uncertain.
We retrospectively analyzed consecutive patients with severe AS and stable CAD, defined as fractional flow reserve ≤0.80, instantaneous wave-free ratio ≤ 0.89, or visual stenosis ≥90%, who underwent TAVI between October 2013 and July 2023. Patients were categorized into two groups: PCI-first and TAVI-first. The primary endpoint was 1-year incidence of major adverse cardiac events (MACE: all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, and unplanned revascularization). The secondary endpoint was 3-year MACE stratified by PCI after TAVI among the TAVI-first group.
Of 1126 TAVI patients, 209 met criteria for concomitant CAD (PCI-first, n = 112; TAVI-first, n = 97). The TAVI-first group had lower frailty and fewer New York Heart Association functional class III/IV symptoms, whereas the PCI-first group had more blood transfusions. At 1 year, the crude incidence of MACE was higher in the PCI-first group, although this difference was not significant after propensity score adjustment (HR 1.62; 95% CI 0.60-5.2; p = 0.36). Among TAVI-first group, patients who underwent PCI after TAVI had a lower incidence of MACE (log-rank p = 0.007), but the 90-day landmark analysis showed no significant difference (0/24 vs. 5/62 events; log-rank p = 0.23).
In patients with severe AS and CAD, a PCI-first strategy was associated with a higher incidence of bleeding and transfusion without improvement in short-term outcomes. A TAVI-first strategy with selective PCI during follow-up may be a reasonable alternative, although the long-term benefit of post-TAVI PCI awaits confirmation in randomized trials.

title: Task Force 4: Clinical Considerations for the Care of Athletes with Genetic Cardiomyopathies.
authors: Sabiha Gati; Michael J Ackerman; Aaron L Baggish; Jonathan H Kim; Benjamin D Levine; Martin Maron; Matthew Martinez; Sharlene M Day
journal: Medicine and science in sports and exercise
abstract: The updated AHA/ACC Scientific Statement on Clinical Considerations for Competitive Sports Participation for Athletes with Cardiovascular Conditions presents the clinical considerations for athletes with genetic cardiomyopathies, including hypertrophic, dilated, arrhythmogenic, and left ventricular hypertrabeculation. This ACSM Official Pronouncement complements the 2020 ACC/AHA Scientific Statement by providing athlete-specific context, practical guidance for shared decision-making, and genotype-informed risk assessment for competitive sports participation, moving away from blanket sports disqualifications. Sports participation recommendations for each condition are tailored to risk levels, symptomatology, and genotype. Regular follow-ups and close surveillance are advised. This evolving approach underscores the importance of individualized care, ongoing research, and the integration of new data to better inform shared decision-making on the risks and benefits of competitive sports in athletes with cardiomyopathies.

title: Preoperative Dependent Functional Status Is Associated with Worse 30-Day Pulmonary Complications in Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement: An Insight from the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program Database From 2005-2021.
authors: Renxi Li; Deyanira J Prastein
abstract:
While current cardiac surgery risk scores do not account for preoperative functional status, it has been linked to adverse outcomes in transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). However, in surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR), preoperative functional status remains underexplored.
To examine the impact of preoperative functional status on 30-day SAVR outcomes to provide insights into clinical decision-making and postoperative care. Methods: Patients undergoing SAVR were identified from the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program database from 2005 to 2021. A 1:3 propensity-score matching was applied to patients with dependent (DFS) and independent (IFS) functional status. Thirty-day outcomes were assessed.
After propensity-score matching, DFS and IFS patients showed similar mortality (11.11% vs. 9.42%, P = 0.39) and major adverse cardiovascular events (9.91% vs. 9.11%, P = 0.66). Patients with DFS had higher risks of pulmonary complications (29.43% vs. 21.64%, P < 0.01) including pneumonia (13.21% vs. 9.21%, P = 0.04) and prolonged mechanical ventilation over 48 hours (25.83% vs. 15.42%, P < 0.01) but lower bleeding requiring transfusion (51.65% vs. 67.49%, P < 0.01). DFS patients were more likely to be discharged not to home (71.52% vs. 47.75%, P < 0.01) and had longer operation time (315.2 ± 130.5 vs. 293.5 ± 119.8 min, P < 0.01) and LOS (18.47 ± 14.30 vs. 15.07 ± 12.83 days, P < 0.01).
While SAVR is relatively safe in eligible DFS patients considering its mortality and cardiac outcomes, it is imperative to emphasize preoperative functional status assessments and closely monitor postoperative pulmonary complications.

title: Aortic valve calcification and one-year paravalvular leak after transcatheter aortic valve replacement: limited role of asymmetry.
authors: Pragati Basera; Roya Anahita Mousavi; Chisom Enwere; Minel Soroa; Edgar Argulian; Leila Alizadeh; Marcos Ferrandez-Escarabajal; Carlo Mannina; Lakshay Chopra; Samin K Sharma; Annapoorna S Kini; Stamatios Lerakis
abstract:
Paravalvular leak (PVL) is a significant complication after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Although total aortic valve calcification (AVC) burden and self-expandable valves are predictors of PVL, the impact of leaflet-specific AVC asymmetry remains uncertain. The authors evaluated the association between AVC asymmetry and mild or greater PVL at 1 year after TAVR and its interaction with valve type.
Patients undergoing TAVR between January 2022 and May 2025 with preprocedural noncontrast cardiac computed tomography and 1-year transthoracic echocardiography were included. Asymmetric AVC was defined as greater than 50% of total AVC on a single cusp.
Among 530 patients (mean age, 79 ± 8 years; 45.5% female), 130 (24.5%) had mild or greater PVL at 1 year. Total AVC was higher in women (1747 vs 1125 AU; P less than .001) and men (2612 vs 2063 AU; P less than .001) with mild or greater PVL, with greater calcification across all cusps. AVC asymmetry was comparable between PVL and non-PVL groups (33.1% vs 41.4%; P = .093). Total AVC independently predicted PVL (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 1.036 per 100 AU; P < .001), whereas asymmetry did not (adjusted OR, 0.912; P = .681). No significant interaction occurred between valve type, AVC asymmetry, and PVL (P = .224).
Total AVC independently predicts mild or greater PVL at 1 year after TAVR, whereas leaflet-specific asymmetry and valve type provide no additional predictive value.

title: Left Bundle Branch Optimized Resynchronization Therapy for Persistent Ventricular Dysfunction After Complex PCI and TAVR.
authors: Esteban Yu Hern Chin; Keng Tat Koh; Asri Bin Said; Ing Xiang Pang; How Kiat Khor; Alan Yean Yip Fong; Tiong Kiam Ong; Yen Yee Oon
abstract:
Severe aortic stenosis with complex coronary artery disease presents challenges in patients unsuitable for surgery. Persistent left bundle branch block (LBBB) after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) may impair ventricular recovery.
A 67-year-old man underwent high-risk left main-left anterior descending percutaneous coronary intervention, complicated by cardiogenic shock and severe left ventricular (LV) dysfunction. Subsequent TAVR achieved favorable valve hemodynamics but was followed by new-onset left bundle branch block and persistent LV dysfunction. Left bundle branch pacing achieved complete correction only at high output. A coronary sinus lead was added for left bundle branch-optimized cardiac resynchronization therapy with a defibrillator (LOT-CRTD). At 3 months, LV function fully recovered with reverse remodeling and marked symptom improvement. Why Beyond the Guideline: Optimal percutaneous coronary intervention-TAVR timing and device strategies for post-TAVR LBBB with LV dysfunction remain poorly defined in current guidelines.
LOT-CRTD may provide effective cardiac resynchronization when isolated left bundle branch pacing cannot achieve optimal correction.
Sequence of PCI-TAVR remained individualized. LOT-CRT is a viable strategy to facilitate ventricular recovery for post-TAVR LBBB.

title: "Whiplash Motion" in Cardiac Intimal Sarcoma With Functional Mitral Stenosis and Dynamic LVOT Obstruction.
authors: Norikazu Oshiro; Takeshi Yoshida; Bunpachi Kakii; Takuya Higuchi; Shinichi Mitsuyama; Masato Furui; Haruo Suzuki; Takashi Kawashima; Shin-Ichi Nakatsuka; Yuki Kubo
abstract:
Cardiac intimal sarcoma (CIS) usually presents as an isolated left atrial mass; pan-left-heart involvement producing simultaneous inflow and outflow obstruction is rare.
A 43-year-old man presented in acute heart failure (B-type natriuretic peptide 948.8 pg/mL; right ventricular systolic pressure 59 mm Hg). Imaging showed a tumor in the left atrium and ventricle: an atrial mass infiltrated the mitral leaflet, causing functional mitral stenosis, whereas a mobile papillary-muscle component showed a "whiplash motion," prolapsing into the left ventricular outflow tract and protruding through the aortic valve in systole. Emergency debulking and mechanical mitral valve replacement followed; histopathology confirmed CIS (mouse double minute 2 homolog/cyclin-dependent kinase 4 positive, mouse double minute 2 homolog-amplified). Although adjuvant carbon-ion radiotherapy provided temporary control, the patient died 20 months later.
We propose the "whiplash motion" sign and highlight the trade-off between mechanical-valve durability and bleeding risk during thoracic radiotherapy.
CIS can cause dual left-heart obstruction through multicomponent tumor dynamics; prosthetic valve choice should anticipate multimodality oncologic management.

title: Extensive Native Aortic Valve Infiltration and Early Bioprosthetic Valve Degeneration in Low-Grade Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia.
authors: Kai Yi Wu; Imran Chaudhry; Russell W Sterrett; Gabor T Gyenes; Matthew F Church; D Ian Paterson; Brian H Sonnenberg
abstract:
Cardiac manifestations of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) are extremely rare, particularly involving valves.
A patient with low-grade CLL presented with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis. Following surgical aortic valve replacement, the patient experienced rapid degeneration of her surgical bioprosthetic aortic valve, necessitating valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement. Re-evaluation of her excised native aortic valve tissue on histology with immunohistochemical confirmation revealed extensive CLL infiltration.
Extensive CLL infiltration of the aortic valve is an extremely rare phenomenon. This case raises the hypothesis that a clonal lymphoproliferative process may contribute to calcific aortic stenosis and possibly early bioprosthetic structural valve deterioration. Additional studies are needed to further evaluate this association.
CLL can rarely affect cardiac valves and may contribute to the development of native valve stenosis. Additional studies are required to determine whether CLL is a risk factor for early prosthetic structural valve deterioration.

title: Understanding pedagogical challenges faced by technology teachers in special needs classrooms
authors: Katane Elizabeth Kekana; Thokozani Isaac Mtshali
journal: Journal of Education and Learning Technology
abstract: Teaching learners with special educational needs requires dynamic and adaptive pedagogical strategies that can lead to social development and academic success. This can be possible if teachers are assisted in mitigating the daily challenges of teaching such learners. This qualitative exploratory case study investigated the pedagogical challenges encountered by two Grade 9 Technology teachers in the Capricorn District of Limpopo Province. This study used Shulman’s Content and Pedagogical Knowledge framework to understand teachers’ challenges. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations; all collected data were analysed thematically. This study found that teachers experienced various challenges, including the emotional labour of teaching, burnout in the LSEN environment and the enactment of instructional knowledge. The study concluded that the sampled teachers displayed weaknesses in lesson planning, activating learners’ prior knowledge, diagnosing errors, achieving curriculum objectives and sustaining engagement. As a result, it was recommended that support through teacher assistants, creative differentiated strategies and enhanced digital-technology literacy to improve outcomes for learners with special needs was imminent.

title: Integration of Biomechanics and Digital Technology: Using Kinovea for Motion Analysis and Learning for Beginner Athletes
authors: Muhammad Nur Hudha; Riezky Maya Probosari; Annisa Nur Khasanah; Supurwoko; Salsabila Kholifahtun Nisa’; Gifran Rihla Gifarka Latief
journal: Journal of Coaching and Sports Science
abstract: Background: The integration of biomechanics with digital motion-analysis technologies has introduced new approaches for examining movement efficiency, kinematic characteristics, and technical patterns in walking and running activities. Kinovea, as an accessible motion-analysis software, provides both visual and quantitative feedback. However, its application in supporting technique development among beginner athletes remains insufficiently explored. Aim: This study aims to describe the use of Kinovea in biomechanics training and examine its contribution to the awareness of kinematic characteristics and movement techniques among beginner athletes. Methods: A descriptive qualitative design involved 72 beginner athletes aged 18–25 years selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected over 16 weeks through interviews, field observations, and motion video recordings analyzed using Kinovea. Kinematic data focused on joint angles, stride behavior, and movement phases during walking, running, and the flight phase. Qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis with NVivo 12, while kinematic results were interpreted descriptively to identify performance patterns and areas for technical refinement. Result: Kinematic analysis showed coordinated joint-angle patterns across all phases. Walking analysis identified arm swing angles of 50.9°–58.8° and leg separation angles of 64.3°–67.2°, indicating a stable gait rhythm. The running analysis revealed knee angles of 68.8°–69.8° and elbow angles of 87.6°–89.1°, indicating efficient propulsive mechanics. The flight phase demonstrated knee angles of 81.2°–87.8° and elbow angles of 80.4°–88.3°, suggesting effective momentum use and postural stability. These measurements supported stride-efficiency assessment and technique evaluation. Qualitative findings revealed that Kinovea enabled athletes to interpret movement phases and identify technical inefficiencies through slow-motion and frame-by-frame visualization. Conclusion: Kinovea supports basic motion analysis by providing clear kinematic information and helping beginner athletes observe and refine their movement techniques. The findings also offer practical value for coaches by enabling more precise identification of inefficient patterns and guiding targeted corrections during early-stage training.

title: A Review of Phishing Detection Techniques Using Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing
authors: Dr. Sunita Dixit
journal: Journal of Global Research in Multidisciplinary Studies(JGRMS)
abstract: The goal of phishing attacks, which rank high among cyber risks, is to steal sensitive information (such as login passwords, financial data, and more) from unsuspecting people and companies. Blacklist, whitelist, rule, heuristic, and signature-based detection methods are no longer suitable due to the rising sophistication of phishing schemes. As a result, ML, DL, and NLP are rapidly becoming into effective instruments for detecting both well-known and brand-new forms of phishing. Background on phishing assaults, old ways of detecting them, and recent advances in intelligent phishing detection are all included in this article. It delves into several machine learning algorithms such as decision tree, LSTM, ANN, CNN, and RNN, as well as deep learning models like KNN, NB, and SVM. Also, natural language processing methods including word embedding, sentiment analysis, text categorization, and tokenization are explored with the aim of detecting phishing material. Presenting a comprehensive, precise, and up-to-the-minute phishing detection system is the ultimate goal of this study, which focuses on machine learning frameworks, performance indicators, present obstacles, and future research directions.

abstract: In the context of increasing complexity of modern network infrastructures and the growing number of cyberattacks, improving the effectiveness of intrusion detection systems is a highly relevant task. The aim of this work is to develop and investigate a hybrid approach to network attack detection based on a combination of signature-based analysis and intelligent machine learning methods.  The research methods include analysis of requirements for anomaly detection systems, comparative analysis of existing solutions, design of a hybrid system architecture, and experimental modeling using multiclass classification of network traffic. The results demonstrate that integrating a neural model with a traditional detection system improves attack detection coverage and reduces the number of false positives.  The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of deploying the proposed architecture in real corporate networks, while the theoretical significance consists in substantiating the effectiveness of a hybrid approach to traffic analysis. Future research directions include adaptive model training and expansion of the range of detectable attacks.

title: Practical Solutions to Common TAVI Complications
authors: Herbert Kroon
abstract: Aortic valve stenosis Calcific aortic valve degeneration mainly affects the elderly population. Approximately 15% of elderly patients have some degree of aortic stenosis (AS)1. Untreated severe AS will lead to heart failure, angina and/or syncope and approximately half of patients will expire within 2 years after symptom onset1, 2. Historically, open heart surgery was the only treatment for severe AS. However, advanced age was a dominant argument to defer surgery. Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) was contrived as a less invasive alternative to surgery and to fulfill this unmet clinical need. After the first-in-human procedure in 2002, TAVI matured into a guideline recommended treatment of symptomatic severe AS in elderly patients across the entire risk spectrum3-7. Peri-procedural embolization Operator experience, improved planning and implantation strategies and multiple device iterations including smaller profile, repositioning ability and outer sealing fabric converted TAVI into a reproducible and relatively safe procedure8. However, the “Big Five” of complications in the modern TAVI era remain 1) access site complications and bleedings, 2) paravalvular leakage (PVL), 3) acute kidney injury (AKI), 4) conduction disturbances including the need for permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) and 5) stroke9. Up to 5% of patients suffer a neurological event after TAVI, mainly within the first 48 hours8, 10, 11. This finding suggests a direct causative role with the transcatheter valve implantation itself. Transcranial Doppler and brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) studies revealed debris embolization towards the brain and new brain lesions after TAVI in the vast majority of patients12-15. Most of these embolizations remain clinically silent at first sight but may be linked to neurocognitive decline and frank dementia16. Embolic protection devices (EPD) have been developed to deflect or capture embolized debris on its way to the brain and may possibly reduce brain lesions and neurological events including stroke and neurocognitive decline. Part I of this thesis adds perspective to the etiopathology of TAVI related stroke and the mechanism of action of the current spectrum of cerebral embolic protection devices. We also present insights into the microscopic analysis of debris that was captured with filters during TAVI procedures. Vascular access and complications 1 TAVI typically requires large bore femoral artery access. By default, larger arteriotomies are at higher risk for access site complications and bleedings. A completely percutaneous approach relies on vascular access closure devices (VCD) to manage the arteriotomy and provide patent hemostasis. TAVI in low to intermediate risk patients is associated with a major vascular complication rate ranging between 2 and 8%4, 11. The conventional closure technique is based on sutures and most access site complications after TAVI procedures are related to closure device failure17. A collagen plug based closure device was introduced as an alternative to sutures. Part II of this thesis addresses vascular complications and provides information on clinical outcomes with collagen plug-based VCD. TAVI-related conduction disturbances Acquired conduction disturbances after TAVI are frequent and may lead to heart failure (re-) admissions and impaired long-term prognosis18-22. The atrioventricular bundle pierces the membranous septum between the right and non-coronary cusp of the aortic valve and surfaces along the left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT), which makes it vulnerable to contact pressure by the implanted transcatheter heart valve (THV) during TAVI23, 24. New left bundle branch block (LBBB) and third-degree atrioventricular block (AV3B) requiring PPI occur in up to a third and quarter of patients, respectively18-22. These conduction disturbances may be transient or remain permanent which is clinically relevant in view of in-hospital stay and overall healthcare costs. Unfortunately, there are no uniform definitions to describe conduction dynamics post-TAVI. Inconsistent reporting makes the interpretation of the literature on this topic challenging. Part III of this thesis will elaborate on what is currently known about the incidence of newly acquired conduction disturbances after TAVI and studies specific features on the baseline and postprocedural electrocardiogram (ECG) to predict conduction dynamics. These insights may help determine the need and timing of PPI and adjust hospital discharge policies.

title: Detecting low left ventricular ejection fraction from ECG using an interpretable and scalable predictor-driven framework: a model development and validation study
authors: Ya Zhou; Tianxiang Hao; Ziyi Cai; Haojie Zhu; Hejun He; Jia Liu; Xiaohan Fan; Jing Yuan
abstract: Low left ventricular ejection fraction (LEF) frequently remains undetected until progression to symptomatic heart failure, underscoring the need for scalable screening strategies. Although artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) has shown promise, existing approaches rely solely on end-to-end black-box models with limited interpretability or on tabular systems dependent on commercial ECG measurement algorithms with suboptimal performance. We introduced ECG-based Predictor-Driven LEF (ECGPD-LEF), a structured framework that integrates foundation model-derived diagnostic probabilities with interpretable modeling for detecting LEF from ECG. Trained on the benchmark EchoNext dataset comprising 72,475 ECG-echocardiogram pairs and evaluated in predefined independent internal (n=5,442) and external (n=16,017) cohorts, our framework achieved robust discrimination for moderate LEF (internal AUROC 88.4%, F1 64.5%; external AUROC 86.8%, F1 53.6%), consistently outperforming the official end-to-end baseline provided with the benchmark across demographic and clinical subgroups. Interpretability analyses identified high-impact predictors, including normal ECG, incomplete left bundle branch block, and subendocardial injury in anterolateral leads, driving LEF risk estimation. Notably, these predictors independently enabled zero-shot-like inference without task-specific retraining (internal AUROC 75.3-81.0%; external AUROC 71.6-78.6%), indicating that ventricular dysfunction is intrinsically encoded within structured diagnostic probability representations. This framework reconciles predictive performance with mechanistic transparency, supporting scalable enhancement through additional predictors and seamless integration with existing AI-ECG systems.

title: Predictors of mortality in patients treated with ECMELLA after cardiac surgery – a single- center experience
authors: Nizar Salah; Matthias F. Bechtel; Justus Thomas Strauch; Vadim Moustafine; Peter Lukas Haldenwang; Dirk Buchwald; Sebastian Loesaus; Simon Becker; Peter Konrad Zahn; Dinah Maria Berres
abstract: Abstract Background Postcardiotomy cardiogenic shock (PCS) remains a serious complication after cardiac surgery associated with high perioperative mortality. Over the last years, the use of veno-arterial extracorporeal life support (VA-ECLS) combined with left ventricular unloading by a microaxial flow pump (ECMELLA) has increased. Data on mortality predictors in patients treated with ECMELLA for PCS remain limited. We aimed to identify factors associated with 30-day all-cause mortality after ECMELLA implantation. Methods We retrospectively analyzed consecutive patients who received concomitant VA-ECLS and a microaxial pump after cardiac surgery at our university center between 2019 and 2024. Clinically relevant surrogate parameters were assessed along with 30-day mortality. Discriminative ability was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Survival was analyzed using Kaplan–Meier estimates with log-rank testing, and predictors of 30-day mortality were identified using univariable and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression. Results Of the 34 patients, 26 (76.5%) died within 30 days. The Model for End-stage Liver Disease (MELD) score was significantly higher in non-survivors than in survivors (18.5 [IQR 10.7] vs. 14.9 [IQR 2.8], p = 0.010). The MELD excluding INR (MELD-XI) score was likewise higher in non-survivors (17.6 [IQR 9.7] vs. 10.2 [IQR 2.6], p = 0.001). Lactate levels were significantly lower in survivors at 12 hours (p = 0.03), 18 hours (p = 0.004) and 24 hours (p = 0.02) after ECMELLA initiation. Discrimination was best at 18 hours (AUC 0.824, p < 0.001). Aortic cross-clamp time was not associated with 30-day mortality when analyzed as a continuous variable; however, an exploratory cutoff of ≥ 63 minutes was associated with increased mortality (HR 3.20, 95% CI 1.34–7.65, p = 0.009). In univariable Cox regression, MELD-XI ≥ 12.5 (HR 2.87, 95% CI 1.13–7.32) and lactate ≥ 2 mmol/L at 18 hours (HR 4.47, 95% CI 1.48–13.52) were associated with 30-day mortality, but neither remained independently associated in multivariable analysis. Conclusions Biological markers, including MELD-XI and lactate, could provide complementary prognostic information before and after ECMELLA implantation, whereas the prognostic value of a prolonged aortic cross-clamp time, observed only in an exploratory threshold analysis, remains uncertain.

title: sabithav507/FusionGAN-Cardio: FusionGAN-Cardio v1.0.0 – Initial Research Release
authors: sabithav507
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Overview FusionGAN-Cardio is a PyTorch-based research framework for synthetic echocardiographic image generation and quality-controlled data augmentation for cardiovascular disease classification. This initial release provides a modular implementation of a disease- and view-conditioned Generative Adversarial Network (GAN), incorporating multi-level feature fusion, attention mechanisms, anatomical constraints, and synthetic-image quality assessment. Key Features Multi-level gated feature fusion architecture. FiLM-based disease and view conditioning. Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM). Conditional global and patch discriminators. Composite adversarial and structural loss functions. Quality-controlled synthetic image generation. Deficit-driven minority disease-view augmentation. Downstream cardiovascular image classification. Independent generative and anatomical evaluation. Comparative baseline implementations. Statistical analysis and reproducibility utilities. Supported Datasets The implementation provides data preparation and evaluation support for: TMED-2 EchoNet-Dynamic CAMUS Datasets must be obtained independently from their respective official sources. No restricted clinical datasets are included in this release. Evaluation and Validation The framework includes: Medical-feature Fréchet distance and KID. Precision and recall metrics. Optional LPIPS and MS-SSIM. Anatomical Dice and HD95 assessment. Downstream classification metrics. Paired statistical comparisons and study-level bootstrap analysis. Software Contents This release includes: PyTorch source code. Model architecture and training modules. Dataset preparation utilities. Configuration files. Baseline implementations. Evaluation and visualization modules. Unit tests. Non-clinical end-to-end smoke testing. Installation and reproducibility documentation. Installation Install the project dependencies using: pip install -e ".[dev,metrics]" Run software tests using: pytest -q Run the non-clinical smoke test using: fusiongan smoke --workdir outputs/smoke_validation Refer to the README.md for complete installation, dataset preparation, training, augmentation, and evaluation instructions. Important Research Disclaimer This software is intended exclusively for research and educational purposes. Image-level aortic stenosis classification and static-frame ejection-fraction prediction are proxy tasks and must not be interpreted as clinical diagnostic measurements. The release provides an executable research implementation and software verification tests. Real-data experimental results and reproduction of manuscript-reported numerical findings require independent dataset preparation and execution of the prescribed experiments. Release Information Project: FusionGAN-Cardio Version: 1.0.0 Release Type: Initial Research Release Framework: PyTorch License: No software reuse license is specified in this release. title: Neuroselective Sensory-Over-Motor Dissociation, Rapid Blockade Onset, and Hemodynamic Autoregulation With 10 μg Intrathecal Dexmedetomidine in High-Risk Orthopedic and Gynecological Surgery: An Observational Analytic Case Series
authors: Muhammad Adiwibowo; Muhamad Farlyzhar Yusuf
journal: Open Access Indonesian Journal of Medical Reviews
abstract: Background: Subarachnoid block gives dense blockade for orthopedic and gynecological surgery, but plain local anesthetics give brief analgesia. Intrathecal dexmedetomidine (DXM), a selective α₂-adrenergic agonist, prolongs block in low-risk patients. Data in high-risk patients are scarce. Objective: To describe block onset, regression, pain scores, and hemodynamic course after 10 μg of intrathecal DXM added to hyperbaric bupivacaine in four high-risk patients. Methods: Four consecutive women (29–73 years) were operated on at Dr. Saiful Anwar Regional General Hospital, Malang, Indonesia (Protocol: CMHC/EC/IRB/2026/0814). Each received 0.5% hyperbaric bupivacaine (15–20 mg) plus 10 μg DXM, by L4–L5 subarachnoid block (Cases 1–3) or combined spinal-epidural anesthesia (Case 4). Onset, hemodynamics, and Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) pain scores were recorded from T₀ to T₄. Results: All patients reached the target block (T6–T10). Sensory onset was ≤ 1 min and Modified Bromage 2 motor block appeared at 3 min; the published mean to Bromage 3 with 5 μg is 11.6 min. Motor inhibition lasted 300 min and analgesia 300–360 min (mean 330 ± 24.5 min), with NRS 0–2 in the first 4 h and 3–4 at 5–6 h. MAP was 70 mmHg in a post-stroke patient. A fall to 50/30 mmHg during bone curettage resolved with 1,000 mL crystalloid and ephedrine. Multimodal and neuraxial analgesia were also given. Conclusion: In four patients, 10 μg of intrathecal DXM was followed by rapid block onset and 5–6 h of analgesia, with no recorded respiratory depression. The series cannot establish effect or mechanism, so controlled studies are needed.

title: Annexins: gatekeepers of endothelial homeostasis and dysfunction
authors: Nerea Méndez‐Barbero; Irene San Sebastián-Jaraba; Hugo Zapata-Polo; María José Fernández-Gómez; Ines Macias-Gamero; José Luis Martín-Ventura; Luis Miguel Blanco‐Colio
abstract: The vascular endothelium plays a central role in maintaining tissue and vascular homeostasis by continuously adapting to biochemical, mechanical, and inflammatory stimuli from its environment. When this adaptive capacity is compromised, endothelial dysfunction develops, driving the onset and progression of a wide range of cardiovascular, metabolic, neurovascular, and inflammatory diseases. Although the molecular mechanisms underlying endothelial dysfunction are complex, growing evidence points to annexins as important regulators of endothelial responses under both physiological and pathological conditions. Annexins are a family of evolutionarily conserved Ca 2+ -dependent phospholipid-binding proteins best known for their roles in membrane organization and cellular signaling. Over the last decade, their functions have expanded considerably, revealing their involvement in processes that are fundamental for endothelial integrity and vascular homeostasis. Emerging studies indicate that annexins influence how endothelial cells respond to inflammatory, oxidative, metabolic, and mechanical stress, thereby shaping vascular barrier function, immune-inflammatory cell recruitment, thrombosis, and tissue repair. In this review, we discuss the current understanding of annexin family members in endothelial biology and examine their contribution to endothelial dysfunction across different disease settings. The available evidence highlights a complex and highly context-dependent network in which individual annexins can either preserve endothelial homeostasis or promote vascular injury depending on the cellular environment and pathological stimulus. A better understanding of their isoform-specific functions may not only advance our knowledge of endothelial pathophysiology but also identify new opportunities for the development of therapeutic strategies targeting inflammatory vascular diseases.

title: Clinical outcomes of TAVI-first versus PCI-first strategies: A meta-analysis of randomized and observational studies
authors: Rodolfo Caminiti; Alfonso Ielasi; Giampaolo Vetta; Antonio Parlavecchio; Dario Pellegrini; Mariano Pellicano; Gabriele Carciotto; Federico Giannino; Andrea Marrone; Davide Besana; Roberto Licordari; Giampiero Vizzari; Antonio Micari
abstract: Background The optimal sequence of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains uncertain. Observational studies suggested lower mortality when PCI was performed after TAVI, but these comparisons may be affected by post-baseline selection. This meta-analysis incorporates the first randomized evidence addressing this question. Methods Randomized and observational studies comparing TAVI-first or PCI after TAVI with PCI-first or PCI before TAVI were included. All-cause mortality was analyzed using adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) from observational studies and an HR approximated from 1-year mortality in the randomized trial. Estimates were pooled using restricted maximum-likelihood random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp inference and stratified by study design. Secondary clinical outcomes were exploratory. Results Six studies were included ( n = 4317): five observational studies ( n = 3331) and one randomized trial ( n = 986). Five studies contributed to the primary mortality analysis, which showed no significant difference between TAVI-first/PCI-after and PCI-first/PCI-before (HR, 0.56; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.20–1.63). Mortality in the randomized trial was 9.5% in both groups. No significant differences were observed for stroke, myocardial infarction, major bleeding, or major vascular complications. Conclusions No mortality advantage was demonstrated for either procedural sequence. In selected patients with stable coronary artery disease and suitable coronary anatomy undergoing balloon-expandable TAVI, TAVI-first appears to be a reasonable alternative to routine upfront PCI, although revascularization and timing should remain individualized. Further direct randomized trials are required.

title: Data underlying the publication: Feasibility of large-scale in silico transcatheter aortic valve implantation trials using a fast-to-evaluate model
authors: Sabine Verstraeten; Marloes van Driel; Robin Willems; Sai Divi; M. J. M. M. Hoeijmakers; Frans N. van de Vosse; Clemens Verhoosel; Wouter Huberts
abstract: This data set contains the data to reproduce the figures from the manuscript: 'Feasibility of large-scale in silico transcatheter aortic valve implantation trials using a fast-to-evaluate model '. The purpose of this study was to assess the feasibility of conducting large-scale in silico TAVI trials using the virtual cohort generator by Verstraeten et al. (2024) in combination with a novel fast-to-evaluate model. This data set contains:1) Matlab scripts to reproduce figures of manuscript.2) Post-processed simulation data needed to reproduce figures of manuscript.3) The 300 male and 450 aortic stenosis .STL geometriesSee the README.txt file for more information about the folders and files in the data set. The simulation data were generated using the novel fast-to-evaluate model that is implemented in Python, as described in the manuscript. The aortic stenosis geometries were generated using the virtual cohort generator, implemented in MATLAB, by Verstraeten et al. (2024). First 300 male and 450 female geometries were generated. The geometries were used as input for the fast-to-evaluate model. Simulations resulting in errors or outliers were discarded. In the end, 200 male and 300 female succesful simulations were used for the analysis of the manuscript. This male/female ratio was equal to the ratio in the clinical trial to which we compared our results.

title: Lipoprotein(a) in Cardiovascular Disease: Integrating Epidemiology, Clinical Guidelines, Molar Measurement, and Emerging Therapies.
authors: Peter E Thomas; Signe Vedel‐Krogh; Florian Kronenberg; Børge Grønne Nordestgaard
abstract: BACKGROUND: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD = myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, peripheral artery disease) and aortic valve stenosis. Plasma concentrations of Lp(a) are >90% genetically determined. Multiple drugs in development reduce lipoprotein(a) by 80% to 98%. While the recently announced topline results, the phase 3 Lp(a)HORIZON trial of pelacarsen did not meet its primary cardiovascular endpoint despite lowering Lp(a), and 3 other cardiovascular outcomes trials remain ongoing. Lipoprotein(a) testing is currently increasing rapidly in many countries. CONTENT: Most guidelines on dyslipidemia and prevention of cardiovascular disease worldwide now advise that Lp(a) should be measured once in all adults, ideally jointly with the first lipid profile ordered. If previous lipid profiles were taken, then Lp(a) should be included in the next lipid profile. Lipoprotein(a) should ideally be measured in nmol/L, and repeat measurements are relevant if drugs are given to lower Lp(a) concentrations, initially at suspected acute coronary syndrome or stroke and again after 1 month, and sometimes in women after menopause. Measuring Lp(a) levels alongside a standard lipid profile provides a more comprehensive initial assessment of a patient's overall cardiovascular risk. Clinical chemistry laboratories that measure lipid profiles should therefore also offer Lp(a) testing. This is easily done as Lp(a) assays can be run on most major clinical chemistry platforms. High Lp(a) is >105 nmol/L (>50 mg/dL). SUMMARY: As use of Lp(a) testing is increasing rapidly worldwide, more clinical chemistry laboratories will likely offer this test locally. Measuring Lp(a) levels alongside a standard lipid profile provides a more comprehensive initial lipid assessment of a patient's cardiovascular risk.

title: Painless Stanford type A aortic dissection presenting with isolated bilateral lower-limb neurological deficits: a case report
authors: Dazheng Fang; Bin Zhao; Jinjie Li; Bing Wu
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Stanford type A aortic dissection (AAD) constitutes a life-threatening cardiovascular emergency. Painless AAD manifesting exclusively as isolated bilateral lower-limb neurological deficits represents an uncommon but recognised presentation of aortic dissection that is prone to misdiagnosis. This case report adds real-world clinical data regarding atypical AAD and delivers practical diagnostic and surgical insights for front-line clinicians. MAIN SYMPTOMS AND IMPORTANT CLINICAL FINDINGS: A 58-year-old Han Chinese female presented with acute-onset bilateral lower-limb numbness and weakness lasting one hour, in the absence of chest, back or abdominal pain. Physical examination uncovered an inter-arm systolic blood-pressure discrepancy together with bilateral lower-limb motor weakness (3/5). Emergency non-contrast chest-abdominal CT identified the aortic double-lumen sign and inward-displaced aortic wall calcified plaques, whereas bilateral distal peripheral pulses remained preserved. MAIN DIAGNOSES, THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTIONS, AND OUTCOMES: Painless Stanford type A aortic dissection complicated by suspected transient spinal cord malperfusion was diagnosed. Following urgent inter-hospital transfer, the patient underwent emergency Bentall procedure combined with aortic arch reconstruction and frozen elephant-trunk graft implantation, with a distal landing zone in the proximal descending thoracic aorta. Her bilateral lower-limb neurological deficits had fully resolved by postoperative day 2. A residual chronic dissection with a thrombosed false lumen persisted distally below the stent-graft and remained stable without interval enlargement. Six-month follow-up confirmed complete functional recovery without residual neurological sequelae or proximal dissection recurrence. CONCLUSION: Undiagnosed painless Stanford type A aortic dissection presenting with isolated bilateral lower-limb neurological deficits is associated with substantial mortality. Routine bilateral upper-arm blood-pressure measurement and recognition of calcification displacement signs on non-contrast CT facilitate early clinical suspicion. Timely confirmation by CTA and urgent comprehensive surgical reconstruction are essential to reverse end-organ malperfusion and optimize neurological as well as survival outcomes.
